Hi Alex / Sarah —

Thanks again for the time earlier — this thread is a short recap + proposed next steps so we can scope the dedicated pilot and sizing validation. I captured the key SLOs and constraints we discussed; please correct anything I’ve missed.

Summary of stated requirements
- User experience: conversational web assistant (desktop + mobile).
- Latency targets:
  - Non-streaming (batch-style requests up to ~128 tokens): p95 <= 400 ms
  - Streaming: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) <= 300 ms, steady-state per-token latency <= 50 ms
- Load profile:
  - Typical concurrent sessions: 60 active sessions (avg); peak concurrent sessions 120
  - Average request rate: ~60 req/s; peak request bursts up to ~180 req/s for short windows
  - Peak observed token throughput (from expected prompt/response sizes): ~6k tokens/s
- Other constraints: US-only region (data residency), pilot must be production-like and include streaming validation harness.

What Redwood proposes for validation (high level)
1) Two-week dedicated pilot (we provide a reserved pool) to run your sample prompt set and streaming flows under controlled load.
2) Validation tests we will run: latency SLOs (p50/p95), streaming TTFB and per-token ramps, concurrency stressing, and tail behavior under burst traffic.
3) Deliverables: sizing matrix (GPU mix recommendations), expected reserved throughput by config, cost estimate, and a short runbook for run-to-failure and fallback policies.

Questions / asks for you to enable sizing and validation
- Please share the sample prompt set and representative token length distributions (or a csv of 1000 recent requests).
- Confirm the acceptable pilot window dates (we suggested Jun 22 start on the call).
- Any must-have model versions or quantization constraints? (e.g., need fp16 only or allow int8 quantized variants)

Next steps I will take
- Produce an initial sizing matrix comparing H100 / A100-80GB / A10G for your workload and reserved throughput targets.
- Schedule a 30-min sync next week to align on the test harness and target metrics.

I attached the call recording and will drop a preliminary sizing matrix and pilot scope in a follow-up message.

Best,

Thanks Ben — this looks right and thanks for the concise list. A few clarifications from our side:

- Streaming TTFB: we actually need to aim for <= 200 ms for TTFB on our most latency-sensitive flows (desktop chat launcher). The 300 ms number is OK for less-critical routes. Can Redwood call out different profiles (latency-critical vs background)?
- Token profiles: I’ll upload a 1k-sample CSV of request/response token pairs by EOD Fri (will include the long-tail examples).
- Models: we prefer an FP16 profile initially but we’re open to quantized (int8) variants if you validate output quality.
- Region: confirm US-East (not multi-region) — our legal team prefers single-region for the pilot.
- Pilot start: Jun 22 is OK, target 2-week run.

We’d like Redwood to include a short run that simulates a sustained 30-45 minute high-burst window to observe tail latency/backpressure behavior. Also please include expected reserved throughput numbers (tokens/s) per GPU SKU in the sizing doc.

I’ll upload the sample prompt set and invite our infra lead to the next sync.

Folks — forwarding Alex’s confirmation. I sketched a first-pass sizing matrix (attached) and pilot scope. High-level recommendation based on their bursty streaming workload:

Sizing summary (initial, conservative)
- Option A (latency-first): 4x H100 (reserved pool)
  - Expected steady-state: ~9k tokens/s aggregate
  - Streaming p95 headroom for TTFB <=200 ms and per-token <=40 ms at target concurrency
  - Good for headroom and shorter tails; higher cost

- Option B (balanced): 6x A100-80GB
  - Expected steady-state: ~7k tokens/s aggregate
  - p95 streaming ~250–300 ms depending on model size and quantization
  - Better cost/throughput for large batch inference if they accept slightly higher latency

- Option C (cost-focused): 10x A10G + optimized batching & aggressive prefix/KV cache
  - Expected steady-state: ~5k tokens/s aggregate
  - Streaming TTFB will be higher on tails; use for non-latency-critical routes or heavy caching scenarios

Reserved throughput and concurrency knobs
- We should recommend a reserved tokens/sec target (e.g., 6k tokens/s) with an autoscale burst buffer for short spikes to 8–9k tokens/s.
- Suggest per-GPU concurrency cap and a target of 12–16 active streams per H100, 8–12 per A100, 6–8 per A10G (these are approximate and we will validate empirically).

Run plan for the two-week pilot
1) Preflight: ingest their 1k sample set, confirm model artifacts, and map token-length distribution.
2) Baseline run: single-GPU microbenchmarks across SKUs (H100/A100/A10G) to collect p50/p95 per-token timings.
3) Full reserved pool validation: run multi-GPU pilot with sustained average load + scheduled 30–45 minute high-burst test.
4) Deliverables: validated sizing matrix (spreadsheet), recommended reserved pool, estimated monthly cost, and an SLA/downtime/fallback playbook.

I attached the sizing matrix (initial) and pilot scope doc. I’ll slot the Jun 22 pilot start as tentative until we confirm final SKU mix and contract terms. Monica — can you draft an initial cost estimate and include a note on discount thresholds (commit level)? Karthik — can you add the specific test harness commands we’ll run so NeuraTech can mirror locally?

Thanks,
Ben

Looks good — a few quick notes and asks before we send the formal pilot proposal:

- Conservative reserved throughput: recommend we size initial reserved tokens/sec ~80% of expected steady-state (so if they expect 6k peak, reserve 4.8k) and enable autoscale to handle short bursts. This reduces cost risk for them and lets us demonstrate autoscale behavior.
- KV / prefix caching: call out KV cache hit assumptions in the matrix; savings are material for repeated prompts (we should include two scenarios: cold cache vs 70% cache hit).
- Quantization: mark A100 numbers as FP16 baseline and include an optional int8 column if Karhtik validates quality delta.
- Security/compliance: they mentioned single-region US-East — loop in security to confirm SOC2 evidence scope; they may request access logs and audit retention.
- Commercial: any pilot commitment over $100k ARR equivalent needs CRO approval — flag in proposal.

I’ll take the lead on the formal cost worksheet and include the conservative reserve suggestion and cache scenarios. Ben — once we get their sample CSV and confirm model artifacts we can finalize the numbers and send the pilot SOW + SLA draft.

-Monica
